items.title: Delhi High Court quashes criminal defamation case against Senior Advocate Pinaki Misra
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has quashed criminal defamation proceedings initiated against Senior Advocate and former Biju Janata Dal (BJD) Member of Parliament Pinaki Misra for calling a lawyer a “crook”. In an order passed on November 17, Justice Sachin Datta observed that the complainant, advocate Siddhartha Singh, had failed to show that Misra's statement lowered his reputation in the estimation of others. The Court allowed Misra' plea and set aside the summoning order passed by a trial court in April 2019 as well as the complaint filed by Singh. "It is also noticed that the impugned order does not consider the context in which the words were allegedly used by the petitioner and the dismissal of the complaint by the Bar Council of Delhi," the Court said. The case arose from an August 2018 report published by The Economic Times about a complaint filed by Singh before the Bar Council of Delhi, alleging professional misconduct by Misra over a conflict of interest. At the time, Misra was a Lok Sabha MP and chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Urban Development. items.title: Bulldozers, chainsaws and ‘parkification’: What’s happening to Delhi’s Central Ridge
items.summary: It's almost a miracle that a sprawling forest exists in the heart of Delhi. Often called the “green lungs of Delhi”, the Central Ridge is an important source of biodiversity in a city increasingly swallowed by urbanisation and smoke. But this forest, tucked away behind Rashtrapati Bhawan, now faces a different kind of threat. According to environmentalist and filmmaker Pradip Krishen, it comes from the government's own intervention. Newslaundry met the author of Trees of Delhi: A Field Guide a week before Diwali to understand what is happening to the forest. The sound of a chainsaw accompanied our conversation for nearly two hours. As we began our morning walk through Budh Jayanti Park, we spotted a JCB standing idle. By the end of our interview, it was at work. Its driver and assistants told us they had been tasked with removing two invasive species: Vilayati Keekar and Subabul . Both grow rapidly and inhibit the growth of other species. The government’s stated aim, then, is forest restoration. items.title: Kerala HC allows RSS-linked teachers' body to hold exam in state schools
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday, November 20, permitted a teachers’ organisation affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to conduct its district-level Young Scholar Exam 2026 in government and aided schools across the state on November 22. The interim order comes despite the state government withdrawing its earlier permission for the examination, following allegations that it could be used to propagate Hindu nationalist ideology among schoolchildren. The examination is being organised by the National Teachers’ Union (NTU), Kerala, the state unit of the Akhil Bharatiya Rashtriya Shaikshik Mahasangh (ABRSM), a teachers’ organisation associated with the Sangh Parivar. It is being conducted in association with Mayilpeeli, a children's magazine published by Balagokulam, an organisation linked to the RSS and known for organising Sree Krishna Jayanti celebrations in Kerala. The involvement of these organisations triggered a political controversy after the General Education Department initially permitted the examination to be conducted in government and aided schools.
